::: {#exm-disaggregated-evaluation}

#### Accuracy for each digit

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
full_by_digit = digit_accuracy(full_net, val_idx)
few_by_digit = digit_accuracy(few_net, val_idx)
by_digit = pd.DataFrame({
    "digit": range(10),
    "images": (y[val_idx][:, None] == torch.arange(10)).sum(dim=0).numpy(),
    "all eights": full_by_digit.to_numpy(),
    "10 eights": few_by_digit.to_numpy(),
})
worst_digit, best_digit = full_by_digit.idxmin(), full_by_digit.idxmax()
fewest_images = by_digit["images"].min()
print(worst_digit, best_digit, fewest_images)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-by-digit
#| tbl-cap: "The accuracy of the two networks of @sol-few-eights on each digit of the validation set."
knitr::kable(py$by_digit, digits = 2)
```

@tbl-by-digit is a [disaggregated evaluation](#def-disaggregated-evaluation) of the two networks,
one row for each digit.
Removing eights lowers the [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) on eights most.
Even the network trained on every eight does better on some digits than on others,
from `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$full_by_digit[[as.character(py$worst_digit)]])` on `r py$worst_digit`s
to `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$full_by_digit[[as.character(py$best_digit)]])` on `r py$best_digit`s.
Each digit has `r py$fewest_images` or more images in the [validation set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-validation-set),
so gaps of a few percentage points between digits could come from the random split alone.

:::
